poc_summary: Crafted a minimal 408-byte TrueType font (cmap format 6 mapping 'T'=U+0054 to glyph 1, a simple 4-point rectangle outline, plus a hand-built GSUB table: ScriptList['latn']->DefaultLangSys->Feature['liga'] whose LookupListIndex array deliberately contains the out-of-range value 1000, while the LookupList itself only declares LookupCount=1) and a standalone poc.c that calls FT_New_Face + FT_Load_Glyph(..., FT_LOAD_FORCE_AUTOHINT) to force the autofit Latin hinter to run (cmap entry for 'T' both selects AF_STYLE_LATN_DFLT and supplies the 'T H E Z O C Q S' blue-zone string used by af_latin_metrics_init_blues, so af_reverse_character_map_new is reached). Compiled with clang -fsanitize=address,undefined against each version's /work/build/libfreetype.a and ran against /tmp/font.ttf. No sanitizer report appeared in post_intro (or any version) because the entire vulnerable code region is compiled out.
explanation: The labelled bug lives in af_reverse_character_map_new's HarfBuzz-based GSUB-lookup iteration (afadjust.c lines ~1357-1504, confirmed by `grep -n ifdef/endif`), and the whole file afgsub.c (which defines af_parse_gsub / gsub_lookups_single_alternate) is wrapped end-to-end in `#ifdef FT_CONFIG_OPTION_USE_HARFBUZZ ... #endif`. In this benchmark's Docker build for all three revisions (pre_intro 9e8b642b1005, post_intro 6a982bde85ea, post_benign), `/work/include/freetype/config/ftoption.h` has `/* #define FT_CONFIG_OPTION_USE_HARFBUZZ */` commented out, `pkg-config --exists harfbuzz` reports NOTFOUND, no system libharfbuzz-dev package is installed (apt-get install fails with a permission error, so it cannot be added), and `nm` on the built static `libfreetype.a` shows zero `hb_*` symbols and no `af_parse_gsub`/`af_reverse_character_map_new`'s GSUB block compiled in. I verified this identically in pre_intro and post_intro (and the libfreetype.a build artifacts are produced the same way for post_benign). Since HarfBuzz support is not compiled into the autofit module in any of the three built revisions, the array `globals->gsub_lookups_single_alternate[]` and the unchecked `hb_set_next()`-returned index that the fix commit bounds-checks are simply never reached — the reverse-character-map function's HarfBuzz block is dead code here, so af_reverse_character_map_new does nothing GSUB-related at all regardless of the font's GSUB contents. I confirmed my crafted PoC does reach af_latin_metrics_init (glyph loads fine under FT_LOAD_FORCE_AUTOHINT, 'T' resolves to glyph 1 via the cmap) and exercises the Latin autofit path, but the specific GSUB-indexing code that the intro/fix commits touch is unreachable in this build configuration. This is a build-environment limitation (missing/undetected HarfBuzz dependency), not evidence about the patch's correctness, and I have no permission to alter the configured build to add the missing dependency (apt lock requires root, and I must not hand-repair the target build). Per the verification guidelines, a build/environment that does not exercise the affected API must be recorded as unknown rather than inferring introduction=no or benign=yes.

oracle.description: Attempted reproduction oracle was an ASan/UBSan heap-buffer-overflow report from reading globals->gsub_lookups_single_alternate[huge_index] in af_reverse_character_map_new; this code path is compiled out (FT_CONFIG_OPTION_USE_HARFBUZZ undefined) in all three built revisions, so no crash signal (or absence of one) can be attributed to the labelled bug.
oracle.target_evidence: ftoption.h: `/* #define FT_CONFIG_OPTION_USE_HARFBUZZ */` (commented out) in pre_intro and post_intro builds; `pkg-config --exists harfbuzz` -> NOTFOUND; `nm libfreetype.a | grep -c ' T hb_'` -> 0; `nm libfreetype.a | grep af_parse_gsub` -> no match; afgsub.c entirely within `#ifdef FT_CONFIG_OPTION_USE_HARFBUZZ`/`#endif /* FT_CONFIG_OPTION_USE_HARFBUZZ */`; afadjust.c's GSUB-indexing block at lines 1357-1504 within the same guard. PoC ran cleanly (exit 0, no sanitizer report) in post_intro despite confirmed glyph load via FT_LOAD_FORCE_AUTOHINT reaching the Latin autofit metrics path.

oracle_assessment.reason: The agent claim lacks a matching admissible three-version oracle.
